page0.text:
Once school ends, I quickly start to head home.
Since all after-school club activities are suspended, students crowd around the campus gate.

page1.text:
I take a cursory look around, and don't see anyone who might be Tohsaka.
Knowing her, she must have gone straight to the Matou house.

page2.text:
"Sakura's...not around, huh."
Without club practice in the afternoon, Sakura can just go home to my house.
We didn't talk about meeting up to walk home together, so she must have gone on ahead.

page3.text:
I take the lonely road up the hill.
It's already been six days since the Holy Grail War started.
Little by little, it feels like life is draining out of the town.

page4.text:
"Argh..."
Just as I reach the top of the hill, I'm struck by a bout of dizziness.
It's like a hollow chill in my head, maybe it's some kind of anemia.
I hear something resonating in my ear.

page5.text:
"What's that noise?"
I cover my ears, but my eardrums still ring.
This isn't a hallucination.
People don't just get hit by unexplained vertigo and tinnitus.
And if they're happening at the same time, then it can only be deliberate.

page6.text:
"Don't tell me something happened at home...!?"
I shake off the dizziness and start running.
Saber's at home.
Even if an enemy attacked, it wouldn't go so easily for them as long as Saber's there...!

page7.text:
The only pair of shoes at the front door belongs to Saber.
"Thank god Sakura's not back yet!"
I don't need to worry about holding back, then.
If this strange situation is happening because of an enemy attack, then we can get through it somehow if only Saber and I are here...!

page8.text:
"Saber, are you all right?"
I rush to the living room.
The instant I arrive,

page9.text: I can't stand anymore, and I tumble to the ground.

page10.text:
"Wha—"
My legs won't do what I want.
The ringing in my ears robs me of my sense of balance.
I'm crushed by an oppressive nausea and chill.
I desperately try to prop myself up on my arms,
when I notice that the color is fading from the marks on my left hand.

page11.text:
...
My mind freezes.
The Command Spells are pale.
Before I process what that means,

page12.text: "I disposed of Saber. I can't let them take over any more Servants."

page13.text: A familiar voice speaks from very close to me.

page14.text:
"..."
I look up, fighting the dizziness.

page15.text: "Sorry, big brother. I wanted to play with you more, but the situation is different now. Blame the flawed Holy Grail, not me."

page16.text:
The ringing invades my brain.
Sound waves that should be imperceptible burrow behind my eyeballs and block off my eyesight.
"But don't worry. I won't kill you right away.
You're going to be my trump card against them. I'll destroy your body here, but I'll swap your mind into one of my puppets.
...Heehee. You won't be able to move anymore, but it beats dying, doesn't it?"

page17.text:
The noise permeates my entire body.
My mind remains as stiff as stone.
In the darkness, deprived of all five senses, I can't even tell how badly it's over for me.
